appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.languageHint: AudioRouter switches language immediately. Device names, tool names and your own session names stay as they are.

updates.heading: New versions
updates.dailyCheck: Check GitHub once a day for a newer version
updates.privacyNote: Reads the public AudioRouter release list on github.com; nothing about you or your audio is sent. If GitHub cannot be reached, AudioRouter retries for up to 12 hours and then waits for the next day. It never downloads or installs an update; the release page opens in your browser. AudioRouter currently publishes prerelease builds.
updates.offDetail: Turn it on to look for new versions.
updates.idleDetail: Check now to look for a newer version.
updates.currentStable: No newer stable version was found.
updates.failedHeadline: Can't check for new versions right now.
updates.installedStableOnly: AudioRouter {{version}} is installed. Only stable releases are checked.
updates.offStored: No result is stored while checking is off.

devices.heading: Audio devices on this PC
devices.help: What Windows offers right now. To use one, add an Input Device or Output Device tool and choose it in that tool's Properties. AudioRouter never changes Windows defaults or volumes. Clear "Show in pickers" to keep a device you never use (a monitor's speakers, a webcam microphone) out of the device lists on this PC.
devices.inactive_one: {{count}} more device is unplugged or disabled in Windows.
devices.inactive_other: {{count}} more devices are unplugged or disabled in Windows.

goalGuide.question: What do you want to do?
goalGuide.step1Recording: In Tools, add Application Capture and choose the exact running process in Properties. Capture includes its process tree, not a browser tab.
goalGuide.step1Voice: Use Set up for Discord to choose your exact microphone and paired voice cable and add optional voice cleanup.
goalGuide.step2Recording: Add a Recorder and connect only that application to it. Leave it unarmed until you deliberately choose to record.
goalGuide.step2Voice: Send only your processed microphone to the voice cable. Keep microphone monitoring muted; do not connect a headphone monitoring branch until you deliberately want it.
goalGuide.deviceHelp: check selected devices in Properties. An available device or running process does not prove audio is arriving.
goalGuide.signalHelp: review the route, then deliberately press Play. Make sound in the selected source and check fresh route meters. Silence needs investigation before continuing.
goalGuide.recordingVerifyHelp: deliberately arm and start the Recorder, stop it, then review the file for the selected app and absence of unrelated apps.
goalGuide.receivingVerifyHelp: open Discord or your receiving app, select the cable's recording end shown by setup, and use its input test. A closed app or correct device selection alone is not a successful audio test.
goalGuide.gamingNote: Keep game and browser audio out of the voice cable. Select headphones for Discord playback and check for duplicate playback separately.
goalGuide.footnote: This guide does not start audio, enable monitoring, arm recording, or change another app. The canvas remains available for advanced routes.

setupWorkbench.otherAppsHelp: AudioRouter does not change settings in Windows or in other apps. To send your processed microphone to Discord, OBS or a game, end the route in an Output Device set to a virtual cable (for example CABLE Input), then choose the matching input (CABLE Output) as the microphone in that app.

deviceTroubleshooting.bindingHelp: Devices chosen here are used only when a single route's Input Device or Output Device tool has no device of its own.

firstRun.heading: Set up a route on this PC
firstRun.connect: Connect to AudioRouter to check available devices.
firstRun.found_one: Found {{count}} input and {{renders}} {{outputs}}. Choose the exact devices in each tool's Properties.
firstRun.found_other: Found {{count}} inputs and {{renders}} {{outputs}}. Choose the exact devices in each tool's Properties.
firstRun.noPair: No complete input-and-output pair is available yet. Connect or enable your audio devices, then refresh this list. AudioRouter never installs audio drivers on its own.
firstRun.step1: Open Tools and add an Input Device and Output Device, or start with Test Signal.
firstRun.step2: Choose an available device in each tool's Properties, then connect the route.
firstRun.step3: Review the route and press Play when you are ready. AudioRouter never changes Windows default devices.
firstRun.virtualCable: To send your microphone to another app, use an existing supported virtual audio device such as VB-Cable or Voicemeeter. Install it separately from its vendor.

quit.unresponsiveMessage: Quit failed: AudioRouter's background service did not answer. Click Quit anyway to close it now. Audio stops, and a recording in progress is recovered the next time you open AudioRouter.
quit.refusedMessage: Quit refused: {{reason}}. Audio keeps playing; stop any recording and try again.
quit.anywayTitle: Close AudioRouter now without waiting for its background service. Recordings in progress are recovered next time.
quit.quitTitle: Stop audio, finish recordings and close AudioRouter (same as the tray's Quit). Unsaved edits come back next time you open it.

sessionSwitch.heading: Stop audio and switch session?
sessionSwitch.description: Switching stops all sessions listed below, including audio used by other apps. Their active recordings will stop and finalize; a finalization failure may leave recoverable partial files. The selected session stays stopped until you press Play.

startup.intro: Start with Windows in the tray (no window) and, if you like, play the selected session and start the API right away. Closing the window keeps audio playing in the tray.
startup.autoplayDescription: Plays the session selected here when AudioRouter starts, for example at sign-in. The tray menu's Play and Stop audio work the same way without opening this window.
startup.autoplayOn: AudioRouter will play the selected session when it starts.
startup.autoplayFailed: Autoplay could not be saved. Try again.
startup.apiHeading: Start the API when AudioRouter starts
startup.apiDescription: Keeps controllers such as a Stream Deck connected after a restart. The API uses the port and network it last started with (Settings, API), or this PC only on port 17891.
startup.apiOn: The API will start with AudioRouter.
startup.apiOff: Start the API from Settings, API, when you need it.
startup.apiFailed: API auto-start could not be saved. Try again.

flowAnimation.heading: Animated connections
flowAnimation.label: Travelling lights on connections
flowAnimation.onHelp: Lights travel along every connection that carries sound.
flowAnimation.focusHelp: The lights pause while you use another program (for example a game on another screen) and resume when you click back in. Colours, glow and meters keep updating.
flowAnimation.offHelp: No travelling lights. Colours, glow and meters still show the level. Uses the least CPU while this window is open.
flowAnimation.closing: Closing the window to the tray stops all drawing.

liveAutosave.heading: Live autosave
liveAutosave.label: Save parameter changes while audio plays
liveAutosave.onHelp: Changes to sliders and tool settings are saved automatically and applied to the playing audio. Changing the route still needs Save.
liveAutosave.offHelp: Parameter changes stay as an unsaved draft until you choose Save. Turning a tool on or off still applies immediately while audio plays.

deviceAccess.dialogTitle: Allow AudioRouter to use your audio devices?
deviceAccess.dialogDescription: To play this session, AudioRouter opens the microphones, speakers and virtual cables in it. It asks once on this computer. You can change this later under Settings → Device access.
deviceAccess.heading: Audio device access
deviceAccess.connectToCheck: Connect to the desktop backend to check audio device access.
deviceAccess.readFailed: Could not read audio device access. Use Check again.
deviceAccess.withdrawnMessage: AudioRouter will ask before opening audio devices.
deviceAccess.confirmFailed: Could not confirm the change. Check again before retrying.
deviceAccess.descriptionReadFailed: The current access could not be confirmed. Check again before changing it.
deviceAccess.descriptionUnavailable: Choose whether AudioRouter may open your session's audio devices when you press Play.
deviceAccess.descriptionAllowed: AudioRouter may open the audio devices of a session when you press Play.
deviceAccess.descriptionAskFirst: AudioRouter asks before opening audio devices the first time you press Play.

troubleshoot.heading: Troubleshoot and recover
troubleshoot.manualHelp: You normally do not need this. Choose each device in the Input Device or Output Device tool's Properties and press Play. Use these controls to check a device's format, reopen a device after Windows reset it, run a deliberate VB-Cable loopback test, or add a loopback source.
troubleshoot.recoveryOwned: Recovery state is owned by the backend.

canvasKeyboard.connectHelp: The same as dragging from one tool to another on the canvas, for keyboard and screen-reader use.
